claim: esbuild build with write:false returns bundled bytes as a caller-owned OutputFile array and publishes nothing.
limitation: No execution of this mode was performed in this pass.

claim: esbuild build with write:true and a destination writes provider-direct durable files and returns no outputFiles.
limitation: Nothing upstream states the file-system state after interruption mid-write.

claim: esbuild transform converts one source unit to code plus map and publishes nothing.
limitation: Not executed in this pass.

claim: analyzeMetafile is a distinct operation that renders a metafile the caller already holds into esbuild's own report text.
limitation: Not executed in this pass.

claim: formatMessages is a public host operation that renders PartialMessage values with esbuild's own terminal formatter.
limitation: Absent from rows E01-E12; discovered from the tagged declarations in this pass.

claim: buildSync with write:false is a distinct blocking operation that refuses plugins and does not use the shared long-lived child.
limitation: Absent from rows E01-E12.

claim: buildSync with write:true is a distinct blocking operation with provider-direct-durable publication and no interruption point.
limitation: Absent from rows E01-E12.

claim: transformSync is a distinct blocking operation.
limitation: Absent from rows E01-E12.

claim: analyzeMetafileSync is a distinct blocking operation.
limitation: Absent from rows E01-E12.

claim: formatMessagesSync is a distinct blocking operation.
limitation: Absent from rows E01-E12.

claim: context acquisition with write:false yields one scoped state owner returning no durable output.
host_applicability: node; bun; deno; browser-wasm (watch and serve unavailable)
limitation: Only context/rebuild/rebuild/cancel/dispose was ever executed, on ubuntu-24.04.

claim: context acquisition with write:true yields one scoped state owner whose every rebuild republishes provider-direct durable files.
limitation: No execution of the direct-write context mode exists at any coordinate.

claim: stop() is a public host operation that terminates the process-global shared native child; it is not a per-context release.
limitation: E12 recorded the native child as a private implementation detail but did not record that its termination is a public exported function.

claim: initialize() is a public host operation guarded by a process-global once-only latch.
limitation: Absent from rows E01-E12.

claim: An explicitly selected esbuild executable run as a scoped child, fed on stdin and read from stdout, is a one-shot operation with no publication.
host_applicability: any host that can spawn a process
limitation: No CLI execution beyond --version and --help was performed.

claim: An explicitly selected esbuild executable run with --outfile or --outdir is a one-shot operation with provider-direct-durable publication.
host_applicability: any host that can spawn a process
limitation: As CLM-015.

claim: An explicitly selected esbuild executable run with --watch is a scoped-process operation exposing only bytes, exit status and durable files.
host_applicability: any host that can spawn a process
limitation: As CLM-015.

claim: An explicitly selected esbuild executable run with --serve is a scoped-process operation owning a network listener.
host_applicability: any host that can spawn a process
limitation: No serve behavior has been executed at any coordinate in this programme.

claim: build with write:true and no destination emits the bundled bytes onto the host process stdout through console.log and returns no output value.
limitation: Absent from rows E01-E12 and from RECONCILIATION section 3; the exact option combinations that reach this path were read from source, not executed.

claim: context.rebuild is a method of the context state owner, not a separate operation: it reuses the captured options and the same buildKey and has no independent acquisition or release.
limitation: Executed only in the sequence context/rebuild/rebuild/cancel/dispose on ubuntu-24.04.

claim: context.watch is a method of the context state owner; it accepts only a delay and resolves once the watch request is acknowledged.
host_applicability: as its owning context; throws on browser-wasm
limitation: Never executed at any coordinate.

claim: context.serve is a method of the context state owner; it returns {port, hosts} and has no stop member, so the server is released only by dispose.
host_applicability: as its owning context; throws on browser-wasm
limitation: Never executed. This is the strongest candidate for promotion to a separate operation, but nothing at 0.28.2 gives it independent acquisition or release.

claim: context.cancel is a method of the context state owner; it resolves on any response, never rejects, and silently resolves after dispose.
limitation: Executed once in one sequence; no race schedule was ever exercised.

claim: context.dispose is the terminal method of the context state owner; it is idempotent through a didDispose flag.
limitation: Idempotence is read from source and was not executed.

claim: PluginBuild.resolve is a sub-operation issued against the owning build's key; it requires an explicit kind and fails before plugin setup completes.
limitation: Never executed.

claim: PluginBuild.onStart registers a per-build callback that may contribute errors and warnings.
limitation: Never executed.

claim: PluginBuild.onEnd registers a per-build callback receiving the full BuildResult; it is the only channel through which a watch-triggered rebuild result is observable.
limitation: Never executed. This is exactly D7 route 2 and it is the only in-process rebuild-result channel esbuild offers.

claim: PluginBuild.onResolve registers a filter/namespace-scoped resolution callback.
limitation: Never executed.

claim: PluginBuild.onLoad registers a filter/namespace-scoped load callback.
limitation: Never executed.

claim: PluginBuild.onDispose registers a cleanup callback that is scheduled with setTimeout after the owning dispose promise has already resolved.
limitation: Never executed. The ordering is read from the shipped implementation and is the basis of LAW-ESB-05.

claim: ServeOptions.onRequest registers a per-request observation callback, and the JS layer installs it only after the serve response has already returned.
limitation: Never executed; whether requests arriving in that window are dropped is unproven.

claim: entryPoints accepts an array of strings, an array of {in, out} pairs, or a record - three distinct request shapes with different output-naming authority.
limitation: None.

claim: stdin supplies one synthetic input unit with contents, resolveDir, sourcefile and loader, and is an alternative to entryPoints rather than a modifier of them.
limitation: None.

claim: write is the request mode that selects between the memory and direct-write operations; it defaults to true on any host with a filesystem.
host_applicability: node/deno default true; browser default false
limitation: The default is derived from streamIn.hasFS in the shipped implementation, not stated in the declarations.

claim: outfile and outdir are the destination request modes; outdir is required for multiple entry points and enables the outbase-relative layout.
limitation: None.

claim: splitting, chunkNames, entryNames, assetNames, outExtension, outbase and publicPath are output-topology request modes; they change what files exist, not whether they are published.
limitation: None.

claim: external, packages, alias, conditions, mainFields, resolveExtensions, preserveSymlinks and nodePaths form the resolution-authority request-mode family; effect-build must forward them without reinterpretation.
limitation: None.

claim: The loader map is a per-extension request mode on build; transform instead takes a single loader value for its one source unit.
limitation: None.

claim: tsconfig and tsconfigRaw are mutually exclusive project-authority request modes; tsconfigRaw overrides all discovered tsconfig.json files.
limitation: None.

claim: plugins is a request mode carrying arbitrary host callbacks; it has no serialisable form and therefore no selected-command peer at all.
limitation: This is a hard lane asymmetry, not a missing feature.

claim: OnResolveResult and OnLoadResult may return watchFiles and watchDirs, so a plugin is a first-class contributor to the watch set of an owning context.
limitation: Never executed; relevant to D7 route 1's requirement that a product-owned watch loop must not guess a provider's source graph.

claim: namespace, filter, suffix, pluginData and import attributes (with) are the plugin addressing request modes; pluginData is opaque caller data round-tripped through a process boundary by an object stash.
limitation: None.

claim: absWorkingDir is a per-request resolution root; it does not change the native child's own working directory.
limitation: Derived from source: the child's cwd is defaultWD, captured at module load.

claim: metafile:true is a request mode on the in-process lanes that adds a result field; --metafile=PATH is instead a modifier that writes a JSON file.
limitation: The two lanes differ in publication, so they must never share a policy or a name.

claim: mangleCache is both a request mode (seed) and a result field (updated decisions) on the in-process lanes; --mangle-cache=PATH is a file-writing modifier on the command lane.
limitation: None.

claim: --watch and --serve are argv modifiers on an ordinary build invocation rather than subcommands, so they compose with each other and with --outdir.
limitation: Because they change lifetime and publication, RECONCILIATION section 1 still promotes them into separate semantic identities.

claim: ServeOptions port, host, servedir, fallback, keyfile, certfile and cors are network request modes with no in-process default beyond an ephemeral port.
limitation: None.

claim: WatchOptions carries exactly one member, delay; there is no callback, no filter and no event option.
limitation: This alone falsifies any claim that context.watch carries a typed event protocol.

claim: bundle is a request mode, and without it esbuild processes each entry point independently rather than producing a graph.
limitation: None.

claim: target accepts a string or an array of engine strings, and supported carries per-feature booleans; at 0.28.2 duplicate engines resolve to the minimum version.
limitation: The duplicate-collision rule is a 0.28.2 behavior change; earlier versions took the last value.

claim: platform selects browser, node or neutral and changes the defaults of format, mainFields and conditions; it is a syntax and resolution-environment axis, not a runtime or architecture target.
limitation: Confirms the imported information-loss ledger: esbuild target is not Bun's OS/arch/libc target and not Node SEA's base-executable coupling.

claim: format selects iife, cjs or esm with no default when not bundling.
limitation: None.

claim: minify and its four component flags, lineLimit, charset, treeShaking, ignoreAnnotations, drop, dropLabels, pure and keepNames are output-shaping modifiers with no lifecycle or publication effect.
limitation: None.

claim: mangleProps, reserveProps and mangleQuoted are RegExp-valued modifiers translated into Go regular expressions by prefixing JS flags, which is a semantic translation effect-build must not re-describe.
limitation: None.

claim: sourcemap accepts boolean, linked, inline, external or both, and sourceRoot, sourcesContent and legalComments are its companions; legalComments:'external' adds a result field to transform.
limitation: None.

claim: jsx, jsxFactory, jsxFragment, jsxImportSource, jsxDev and jsxSideEffects are the JSX modifier family.
limitation: None.

claim: define, inject, banner and footer inject caller-authored text or modules; banner and footer are per-type records on build and plain strings on transform.
limitation: None.

claim: logLevel, logLimit, logOverride, logStyle, color and absPaths are diagnostics-presentation modifiers; logStyle:'visualstudio' exists only from 0.28.2.
limitation: None.

claim: allowOverwrite authorises esbuild to write over its own input files; without it, 0.28.2 protects inputs by writing no files at all when a build error is encountered.
limitation: The protection is stated for build errors only; the changelog says nothing about interruption.

claim: --analyze and --analyze=verbose are CLI modifiers that add a report to stdout; there is no in-process modifier peer, because the in-process lane exposes analyzeMetafile as an operation instead.
limitation: A mixed row would classify 'analyze' once; it is a modifier in one lane and an operation in the other.

claim: --watch-delay is the command-lane peer of WatchOptions.delay.
limitation: None.

claim: --watch=forever is a modifier that detaches the watch lifetime from stdin closure.
limitation: Never executed; the stdin-closure default is stated by the binary's own help text.

claim: --cors-origin is the command-lane peer of the in-process cors object and accepts no structured form.
limitation: None.

claim: BuildResult.errors and BuildResult.warnings are Message arrays; a failed build instead rejects with a BuildFailure Error carrying the same two arrays.
limitation: None.

claim: Message carries id, pluginName, text, location, notes and an unmodified caller-supplied detail; Location carries file, namespace, 1-based line, 0-based byte column, byte length, lineText and suggestion.
limitation: Column and length are byte offsets, not code-point offsets; any effect-build rendering that assumes characters is wrong.

claim: BuildResult.outputFiles is present only when write is false, and its type makes that conditionality explicit at the type level.
limitation: None.

claim: OutputFile carries path, contents as a Uint8Array, hash as a string, and a lazily decoded readonly text getter that re-decodes when contents is replaced.
limitation: The hash's algorithm is not declared anywhere in the declarations, so it cannot serve as a D12 algorithm-qualified digest as-is.

claim: Metafile.inputs records per-input bytes, imports with kind and optional external/original/with, and optional format; Metafile.outputs records bytes, per-input byte attribution, imports (including the synthetic file-loader kind), exports, entryPoint and cssBundle.
limitation: This schema must be preserved verbatim; normalising it away is the exact information loss the imported ledger warns about.

claim: TransformResult carries code, map, warnings, conditional mangleCache and conditional legalComments; it has no output-file, metafile or errors field.
limitation: None.

claim: ServeResult carries exactly port and hosts.
limitation: There is no stop member, so the result is an observation and not a handle.

claim: ServeOnRequestArgs carries remoteAddress, method, path, status and timeInMS, where timeInMS is time to generate the response rather than to send it.
limitation: None.

claim: ResolveResult carries errors, warnings, path, external, sideEffects, namespace, suffix and pluginData.
limitation: None.

claim: analyzeMetafile returns one plain string with no declared machine contract.
limitation: None.

claim: On the command lane the only machine-observable results are exit status, stdout bytes and stderr bytes; there is no BuildResult, no Message array and no metafile object.
limitation: REC-006 remains falsified: no typed event or diagnostic may be derived from these bytes.

claim: esbuild@0.28.2 publishes sha256 digests for its platform binaries under the esbuild.binaryHashes key, and the @esbuild/linux-x64 binary's computed digest matches its published entry exactly.
host_applicability: linux-x64 verified; 22 other hashed cells unverified
limitation: Verified at exactly one platform cell in this pass.

claim: Three of the 26 platform packages - @esbuild/android-arm, @esbuild/android-x64 and @esbuild/openharmony-arm64 - have no entry in esbuild.binaryHashes, and they are exactly the WebAssembly-fallback platforms.
limitation: The coherence relation therefore has a hole on exactly the platforms where the 'native binary' is a WebAssembly module executed by node.

claim: esbuild's binary integrity check runs only on the two install-time fallback acquisition paths; a binary resolved normally through require.resolve is never hashed, and the whole postinstall step is skipped under --ignore-scripts.
limitation: A published hash existing is not the same as it having been checked in any given install.

claim: The JavaScript API refuses to start when the first packet from the child does not carry the host package's exact version string, raising 'Cannot start service: Host version ... does not match binary version ...'.
limitation: This is the runtime half of package/API/native-binary coherence. It fires at first use, not at layer acquisition, and it throws inside a stdout data handler rather than rejecting the pending request.

claim: The installed form of node_modules/.bin/esbuild is decided at install time: on non-Windows, non-yarn, non-WASM installs, install.js hardlinks the native binary over the node shim, so the same path is sometimes a Node process wrapping a child and sometimes the native executable itself.
limitation: Signal delivery, process-tree shape and exit reporting differ between the two forms. Any selected-command operation must record which form it selected.

claim: When ESBUILD_BINARY_PATH is set at install time, install.js rewrites both bin/esbuild and lib/main.js in place, so the installed library bytes differ from the published tarball bytes.
limitation: A digest of the published tarball therefore does not authenticate an installed tree.

claim: The JavaScript API refuses to run when its own file has been bundled, detected by checking that __filename ends in main.js and __dirname ends in lib.
limitation: Any effect-build package that bundles its dependencies must mark esbuild external.

claim: The CLI loader enumeration accepted by the native binary includes global-css and omits default, while the TypeScript Loader union includes default and omits global-css; the JavaScript layer validates loader values only as strings, so the declarations are narrower than the binary in one direction and wider in the other.
limitation: Two official artifacts of the same version disagree. Which one is authoritative for a given call was not executed.

claim: GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr is an operation-, lane- and host-specific hole: esbuild's development server allowed path traversal through backslashes on Windows, first patched in 0.28.1.
limitation: The advisory page names 0.27.3 while the imported compatibility matrix records >=0.27.3 <0.28.1; the lower bound is unresolved.

claim: GHSA-gv7w-rqvm-qjhr is a host-specific hole affecting only esbuild's Deno module, which downloaded and wrote executable binaries without integrity verification from >=0.17.0 until 0.28.1, honouring NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY.
limitation: Not applicable to the node or bun hosts effect-build composes; recorded so a future Deno-hosted esbuild composition is not admitted by inheritance.

claim: Between 0.17.0 and 0.28.1 inclusive, esbuild printed the input-overwrite error but wrote the file anyway; 0.28.2 restored the protection.
limitation: A behavioral hole spanning a wide version range, discoverable only from release notes.

claim: Package version, declaration bytes, platform-package identity, native binary digest and Go toolchain revision are five separate facts that together constitute esbuild's provider-implementation-identity; at 0.28.2 the Go toolchain moved from 1.25.7 to 1.26.1.
limitation: RECONCILIATION section 1 already forbids substituting a version string for this identity; this row enumerates the actual components.

claim: esbuild.version is a module-level string export that reports the JavaScript package's own version, not the native binary's.
limitation: Reading it proves nothing about the binary; only the first-packet check (CLM-078) or executing the binary's --version does.

claim: PluginBuild.esbuild hands every plugin a complete copy of the library, including context, build, buildSync, transform, transformSync, formatMessages, analyzeMetafile, initialize and version.
limitation: A plugin can therefore re-enter the API, including the blocking sync variants, from inside a build. effect-build cannot bound plugin authority.

claim: The native binary reports its own version through --version and its complete flag surface through --help.
limitation: Executed at exactly one platform cell (linux-x64, digest e1698a3d...).

claim: allowOverwrite plus an outfile pointing at an input turns a build into an in-place mutation of the caller's source tree.
limitation: This is the only mutation of pre-existing caller-owned content esbuild performs; it is not a signing or artifact-lineage operation.

claim: --metafile=PATH and --mangle-cache=PATH mutate or create caller-selected JSON files as a side effect of a build.
limitation: Overwrite behavior for a pre-existing file was not executed.

claim: ESBUILD_BINARY_PATH overrides the selected native binary at both install time and run time, with the single literal /usr/bin/esbuild rejected.
limitation: An ambient-authority input outside effect-build's selected-tool model that can silently change which binary runs.

claim: ESBUILD_WORKER_THREADS=0 disables the worker-thread path for the sync variants, changing them from a worker call to an execFileSync child.
limitation: None.

claim: ESBUILD_MAX_BUFFER raises the 16 MiB stdout ceiling of the synchronous execFileSync path.
limitation: Only affects the rejected sync operations.

claim: The shared native child is created with child_process.spawn and stdio ['pipe','pipe','inherit'], so its stderr is the host process's stderr.
limitation: effect-build cannot capture, redirect or attribute anything esbuild's native child writes to stderr in the in-process lanes.

claim: The shared native child inherits process.cwd() as captured at module load into defaultWD, and it is unref'd so it does not hold the host event loop open on its own.
limitation: Bun's child_process and unref semantics are unproven at any coordinate.

claim: Sufficiently large transform inputs are staged through a temporary file at os.tmpdir()/esbuild-<64 hex chars> and unlinked by the reader.
limitation: Cleanup on failure or interruption is unproven; the threshold was not determined.

claim: The sync variants default to a worker_threads Worker created from the library's own __filename with execArgv explicitly emptied.
limitation: Only affects the rejected sync operations.

claim: Under Yarn PnP the native binary is copied out of a .zip into node_modules/.cache/esbuild before it can be executed.
limitation: A cached copy's digest is not re-verified against esbuild.binaryHashes.

claim: On the three WebAssembly-fallback platforms the selected command is node running a WebAssembly module, not a native executable.
limitation: Not among the five certification hosts of D13; recorded so no support claim is inherited.

claim: esbuild's postinstall performs network acquisition (npm install, then a direct https GET from registry.npmjs.org) when the platform package is missing.
limitation: This is installation-phase behavior of a third-party dependency, entirely upstream of effect-build's evaluation phases. It is not an effect-build fallback and must not be described as one, but the resulting binary's provenance differs from the ordinary path.

claim: esbuild build output can serve the NodeMainProgram sealed-main role; one exact direct-main fixture previously matched between Bun and esbuild while imported-module semantics diverged.
limitation: Ship-if-pass under D8; the adversarial matrix in R5 has not been run.

claim: The esbuild context conformed to the IncrementalNodeMain profile in one recorded execution, with lifecycle context/rebuild/rebuild/cancel/dispose and content changing between rebuilds.
limitation: The same receipt records afterCloseRejected for Rolldown but not for esbuild, so post-release rejection is unobserved for this provider. D15 keeps the profile gate independent of any provider package gate.

claim: esbuild build output is a candidate producer for the BrowserModulePayload role.
limitation: Lower confidence than CLM-102; no esbuild browser-role execution exists at any coordinate.

claim: LAW-ESB-01: the native child is process-global and shared by every one-shot call and every live context in the host process, including those created by code effect-build does not own; therefore no effect-build scope may terminate it.
limitation: Follows from the shipped implementation. It is the reason ESB-OP-13 is rejected.

claim: LAW-ESB-02: esbuild's native child is not an effect-build command lane; it is owned, spawned, versioned and terminated entirely by the esbuild package, and effect-build must neither model it as a selected command nor claim authority over it.
limitation: Restates E12's 'do not double-own' with the mechanism now established from source.

claim: LAW-ESB-03: CLI --watch and --serve are not semantic twins of context.watch and context.serve; they differ in result channel, options record, termination channel and engine sharing, and must never share a name, a type or a policy.
limitation: None.

claim: LAW-ESB-04: rebuild, watch, serve, cancel and dispose remain methods of one scoped state owner; at 0.28.2 none of them has an independent acquisition, an independent release, or a key of its own.
limitation: The falsifier is explicit: an upstream handle that can be released without dispose would promote that method to an operation.

claim: LAW-ESB-05: dispose() resolving does not mean plugin cleanup finished - onDispose callbacks are scheduled with setTimeout after the dispose promise settles - so a Scope finalizer that awaits dispose must not claim plugin resources are released.
limitation: Read from the shipped implementation; the resulting window has never been measured.

claim: LAW-ESB-06: rebuild() coalesces - concurrent calls share one promise and yield one result value - so effect-build must not promise per-call build identity, ordering, or a one-to-one mapping between calls and builds.
limitation: Never executed under concurrency.

claim: LAW-ESB-07: cancel() is best-effort and unfailing - it resolves on any response, never rejects, and silently resolves after dispose - so it may not be surfaced as a cancellation guarantee.
limitation: Never executed against an active build.

claim: LAW-ESB-08: post-dispose behavior is untyped - didDispose guards only cancel and dispose, so rebuild, watch and serve after dispose reach the native child with a deleted key and their outcome is decided there, not by a typed JavaScript error.
limitation: This is the single largest empirical hole in the esbuild surface and P-ESB-02 exists to close it.

claim: LAW-ESB-09: provider-direct-durable is the only truthful publication class for esbuild's write modes; there is no staging, no atomic rename, no all-or-nothing set and no rollback, and the universal stage/verify/atomic-publish sequence must not be applied to them.
limitation: Consistent with the gates' lifecycle-specific-publication requirement and Law D2 of the lifecycle lane.

claim: LAW-ESB-10: esbuild offers no cancellation for any one-shot operation; Effect interruption stops the fiber awaiting the promise while the native child keeps working, and documentation must say exactly that.
limitation: Matches the lifecycle lane's one-shot-without-cancel row.

claim: LAW-ESB-11: esbuild's native stderr is inherited by the host process and its stdout write path goes through console.log, so effect-build owns neither stream and must not promise captured or attributed provider diagnostics in the in-process lanes.
limitation: None.

claim: LAW-ESB-12: the sync variants are non-interruptible by construction; wrapping a blocking call in an Effect that advertises interruption would be a false promise, which is why all five are rejected rather than deferred.
limitation: None.

claim: LAW-ESB-13: a selected esbuild command must be identified by the content of the file actually selected, because the same conventional path may be a node shim or the native binary depending on install-time conditions, and ESBUILD_BINARY_PATH can redirect either.
limitation: This is the esbuild-specific instance of D9's launch-boundary reauthentication requirement.

claim: LAW-ESB-14: the CLI cannot report its bound serve address except as human text, so a command-lane serve operation is honest only when the caller pins an exact port; deriving the port by parsing stdout is forbidden by REC-006 and D7.
limitation: This is the reason ESB-OP-18 is deferred rather than shipped.

claim: LAW-ESB-15: metafile production is a result field of a build and analyzeMetafile is a separate operation; on the command lane both collapse into modifiers (--metafile=PATH writes a file, --analyze prints text), so the two lanes must not share a name or a policy.
limitation: This is the worked example of a mixed row that decomposes into an operation, a result field and two modifiers at once.
